page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.48xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by 192 dedicated physical cores of the ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor architecture running at 2.7 GHz. The instance features 1536.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with 11400 GB of local NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and network performance is supported by a 50 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 314412.22 and Geekbench multi-core reaching 20633.0. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with read-only small block cached speeds at 21309.29 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 411.52 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET benchmarks also rank in the top tier, with Redis achieving 361.71 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category. LLM inference prompt processing for small models is relatively weak at 280.46 tokens per second, though medium model prompt processing is strong at 191.58 tokens per second.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the r8gd.48xlarge is driven by its high resource density, combining massive ARM-based core counts with substantial local NVMe storage and memory. This hardware profile is optimized for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads such as large-scale database operations, Redis caching layers, multi-threaded data decompression, and static web serving. The lack of hyperthreading ensures dedicated physical core allocation, which benefits predictable multi-threaded execution but limits workloads reliant on high single-thread clock speeds or specialized x86 instruction sets.

It features 1536.0 GB of RAM, 11400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth performance, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 314412.22 and Redis SET operations reaching 361.71 million operations per second. Single-core performance remains average, as shown by Geekbench single-core scores. This instance provides high resource density, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for large-scale database deployments, caching layers, and multi-threaded data processing. It is best suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and static web serving.
